cards.text: Back in Luke 6:13, Jesus picked twelve of His disciples and named them apostles. Now He calls the Twelve together. I bet they figure it's a staff meeting, and friend, it is NOT a staff meeting.

cards.question: Jesus gives the Twelve power and authority over all ___.
Along with authority over all demons, Jesus also gives the Twelve power to cure diseases.

cards.text: Then Jesus sends them out, and one of their jobs is to heal the sick. Day one on the job, no training video, no name tag, and they're out there doing what Jesus does!

cards.question: Jesus also sends the Twelve out to proclaim the same thing He's been proclaiming from town to town since Luke 8:1. What is it?

cards.text: Now Jesus tells them what to take on the trip. Village after village, on foot. You'd think a trip like that needs some supplies.

cards.question: Jesus tells the Twelve to bring bread and money for the journey.

cards.text: Jesus says, "Take nothing for the journey," and that means no staff, no bag, no bread, no money and no second tunic. Friend, I pack a spare apron just to walk across my own bakery.

cards.question: When the Twelve enter a house in a new area, how long does Jesus tell them to stay there?
If a town doesn't welcome the Twelve, what does Jesus tell them to do as they leave?

answers.text: Shake the dust off their feet
Tear their cloaks at the town gate
Call down fire on the town

cards.text: Jesus says it's a testimony against them. Baker, after all my years in a junk drawer, I could shake off enough dust to testify against a WHOLE city.

cards.question: So the Twelve set out and go from village to village. What do they do everywhere they go?

answers.text: Preach the gospel and heal people

cards.text: Word gets around. Herod the tetrarch, the ruler over Galilee (Luke 3:1), hears about all that's happening.

cards.question: When Herod the tetrarch hears about all that's happening, he is ___.

cards.text: Here's the problem: people can't agree on who Jesus is. Some say John the Baptist, the man Herod locked up in prison back in Luke 3:20, has risen from the dead.

cards.question: Others say ___ has appeared, the prophet who went up into heaven in a whirlwind back in 2 Kings 2:11.

cards.text: And still others say a prophet of old has arisen. Three groups, three answers, and nobody budging, friend, that's the dead batteries in my old junk drawer arguing over who's got the most charge left.

cards.question: Herod brings up John the Baptist himself. What does Herod say he did to John?

answers.text: He sent him away to Egypt

cards.question: After Herod asks, "but who is this man I hear such things about?" he gives up on trying to see Jesus.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus has been proclaiming the kingdom of God 'since Luke 8:1,' which makes Luke 8:1 the starting point. Luke already shows Him preaching the kingdom of God earlier, in Luke 4:43 ('I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well'). Luke 8:1 doesn't say it's where this preaching began.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: The card cites only Luke 9:3, but 'Village after village' is told from Luke 9:6. It should cite only what it tells, or drop the Luke 9:6 detail.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Card 15 already says people claim John 'has risen from the dead,' so the baker knows John is dead. That rules out the wrong answers 'He released him from prison' and 'He sent him away to Egypt,' because neither involves John dying. 'He beheaded him' is the only answer left. The wrong answers need to be believable ways John could have died.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
